hedges.reason: For Ricketts to lose in an R+ farm state, the national midterm swing has to be large enough that Republicans also lose the House. An R Senate plus R House sweep and an Osborn win are close to mutually exclusive.
This pays when Republicans do not win the House. It is the same national-wave mechanism as E37.4, expressed on the House side through a separate contract.

Alaska is another red state with a strong non-Republican challenger in Peltola. The same anti-incumbent, rural-economy backlash that would lift Osborn would also threaten Sullivan. The link is weaker than the House legs, so I make no claim on it.

claims.reason: Nebraska votes well to the right of the median House seat. A national environment strong enough to beat a well-funded Republican incumbent there moves the many marginal House seats even further, so Republicans cannot keep the House, and the R-R sweep fails.

The mechanism is the same: a uniform swing large enough to flip Nebraska for an independent flips the House majority. That leaves 'Republican Party wins the House' false whether or not the ACA credits were extended.
